- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The education system in Japan has undergone significant changes over the past century, including a centralized system in the early 1900s focused on national identity and rote learning.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] After World War II, Japan introduced a new education law in 1947, changing the system to a 6+3+3 structure with compulsory education until the ninth grade.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recent challenges in the Japanese education system include a declining birth rate, pressure on students to perform well on exams, and a widening education gap between urban and rural areas.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Japanese government has implemented measures to improve the education system, including earlier English education and promoting digital literacy.
- [USER] User inquired about the impact of exam pressure on students' overall well-being and mental health.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The pressure on students in Japan leads to high levels of stress, anxiety, and depression, often referred to as "exam hell."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Physical health problems linked to exam pressure include headaches, fatigue, and weight loss, with extreme cases leading to suicide.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Japanese government has recognized these issues and introduced measures to support mental health, including increased support from school counselors and promoting extracurricular activities.
